note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
    - Main complaint: Soreness and cracked skin on hands, particularly palms.
    - Trigger/exposure: Works as a housekeeper in a hotel; frequent use of cleaning products without consistent glove use.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
    - Onset: 3–4 months ago, following switch to new housekeeping job.
    - Progression: Gradually worsened; now painful enough to impair ability to work.
    - Recent course: Unable to work for past 3 days due to symptoms.
- ENT symptoms:
    - Denies: No reported throat tightness/swelling, voice changes, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear or neck symptoms.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
    - No prior similar episodes reported.
    - Has tried E45 cream and an oral antihistamine (specific type, dose/route/frequency not documented) without benefit.
    - No prior hospital or injection treatments for this issue.
- Allergies and current medications:
    - No known drug or general allergies.
    - Current medication: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
    - Works as a hotel housekeeper; not always uses gloves with cleaning chemicals.
    - No reported tobacco use.
    - Minimal alcohol intake (a couple of pints per week).
    - No comment on accompaniment/supervision.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
    - Hands: Cracked, dry skin with occasional bleeding when scratched, primarily on palms.
    - No mention of swelling or other visible findings on face, lips, tongue, uvula, or neck.
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
    - No breathing difficulties or noisy breathing reported or observed.
- Mental status and associated features:
    - Alert, oriented; no dizziness or syncope.
- Vitals and examination findings:
    - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person:
    - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
    - Likely occupational irritant or contact dermatitis of the hands, likely related to exposure to cleaning chemicals without gloves.
    - No evidence of acute oropharyngeal, facial, or airway involvement.
    - No systemic allergic features reported.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
    - Strongly advised patient to avoid triggers: must wear gloves at all times when handling cleaning products.
    - Prescribed topical steroid cream (specific type, dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Prescribed stronger emollients to be used 3–4 times daily to moisturize hands for 1–2 weeks.
- Specific instructions:
    - Advised to resume use of emollients as directed and begin topical steroid.
    - If not improved within 1–2 weeks, or if symptoms worsen (spread of rash, increasing dryness, inability to work), to return for reassessment sooner.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
    - Advised to return if condition worsens, symptoms spread, or do not improve after 10–14 days.
- Follow-up:
    - Prescription to be sent to pharmacy.
    - Review advised in 1–2 weeks or earlier if worsening.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
    - Details of topical steroid (type, dose, frequency) not specified.
    - Details of prior antihistamine use (type, dose, frequency) not specified.
    - Comprehensive allergy list for non-medication/occupational exposures not fully detailed.
    - No examination findings or vitals recorded.
    - No documentation on prior skin conditions, eczema, or dermatitis other than patient self-report.
    - No mention of auto-injector or anaphylaxis plan (not indicated but expected for acute ENT/allergy workup).
● Internal conflicts from transcript:
    - None identified.
● Transcript quality:
    - Clear, with minimal background noise. Relevant clinical information extracted; no major inaudible sections.
